newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold eases, tags world trend.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold eases, tags world trend.

text.p: Gold 24 carat closed 20 rupees lower at 4,500 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,520 rupees as fresh losses in the world market prompted selling, dealer said.
Sluggish seasonal demand and speculation the Indian government may further liberalise gold import policy also subdued the market sentiments.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.64 grammes) closed 200 rupees lower at 52,700 rupees per piece after gaining 300 rupees last week.

Meanwhile silver (.999) closed 30 rupees higher at 6,470 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,440 rupees as uptrend in the world market helped prices to recover early losses towards the close.

Silver opened lower at 6,425 rupees per kg in the early trade on fresh arrivals but later on bounced back on an uptrend in the world market as well as stray festival support. Silver was up by 115 rupees per kg last week.
